method: Read every complete available English caption export for the selected lessons. Review evaluates content and instructional sequence, not visual production or successful embedded playback. Public captions may contain transcription errors. Full transcripts remain ignored and are not redistributed.

videos.title: Fuses and HRC Construction: Identify the Protective Devices
videos.flowRationale: Identify physical fuse families before time/current behaviour.
videos.qualification: Historic BS examples support identification. Use marked ratings and actual characteristics; fuses can fail. HRC filler cools and de-ionises the arc. A fixed fusing factor is not a universal selection rule.

availability.publicTitle: Different Types of Protective Devices BS 3036, BS 1361, BSEN 60898 and BS 88 Fuses

videos.title: Fuse Operation: Current, Heating and Time
videos.flowRationale: Optional heating demonstration immediately reinforces the fuse foundation.
videos.qualification: This glass-fuse experiment illustrates heating and time, not HRC breaking capacity. Rated current is not an instantaneous operating threshold.

availability.publicTitle: Fuses: When Breaking Something Is a GOOD Thing! 💥

videos.title: MCB Fundamentals: Thermal Trips, Magnetic Trips and B/C/D Curves
videos.flowRationale: Progresses from thermal and magnetic mechanisms to curves and fault levels.
videos.qualification: Select the curve from load inrush and required disconnection, rather than the building label. Use current tables, manufacturer data and verified fault levels; the UK examples are historical.

availability.publicTitle: The Complete Guide to MCBs - Miniature Circuit Breakers

videos.title: MCCB Fundamentals: Frame Size, Trip Settings and Breaking Capacity
videos.flowRationale: Frame and trip ratings follow the MCB foundation; prepares the same presenter’s ACB explanation.
videos.qualification: Frame size is not the overload setting. The 800 A crossover and pickup ranges are examples. Check rated voltage, Icu/Ics and manufacturer coordination. Ground-fault tripping is not necessarily personnel RCD protection and must satisfy the design.

availability.publicTitle: Episode 1 - What is a MCCB Moulded Case Circuit Breaker, LSIG, ICS, ICU? Explained by a M&E Engineer

videos.title: ACB Fundamentals: Trip Units, Draw-Out Construction and Releases
videos.flowRationale: Direct sequel to the MCCB lesson: trip units, construction and releases.
videos.qualification: Read after the MCCB lesson. Ratings, coil voltages, undervoltage thresholds and maintenance-mode settings are model-specific. Recognise the functions here; actual operation and withdrawal require the approved equipment procedure.

availability.publicTitle: Episode 2 - What is a ACB, Air Circuit Breaker, Trip Units, draw-out explained by a M&E engineer!

videos.title: ACB Component Recognition: Siemens 3WL Example
videos.flowRationale: Optional manufacturer recognition consolidates the preceding ACB explanation.
videos.qualification: A product example for recognising the trip unit, charging motor, releases and auxiliary contacts. Features and ratings vary by model.

videos.title: Residual-Current Protection: Principles and Types AC, A, F and B
videos.flowRationale: Starts with residual-current balance before waveform classifications.
videos.qualification: 30 mA reduces shock risk; it is not a safe current. DC-tolerance figures are not residual trip-current ratings. Select waveform type for the actual load and manufacturer requirements; verify current local rules.

availability.publicTitle: The Complete Guide To RCDs - Residual Current Devices

videos.title: RCCB and RCBO: Separate and Combined Protection
videos.flowRationale: Distinguishes the RCD family from combined overcurrent protection.
videos.qualification: An RCCB needs appropriate overcurrent protection. An RCBO combines residual-current and overcurrent protection; select its poles, ratings and fault duty for the circuit.

availability.publicTitle: What's the difference between an RCD and an RCBO? - Circuit protection.

videos.title: Three-Phase RCDs: Current Balance, Unequal Loads and Neutral Connections
videos.flowRationale: Applies residual-current balance to three-phase and neutral conductors.
videos.qualification: Sense every live load conductor, including neutral where used; unequal phase loads alone do not cause residual current. A three-wire load may need no load neutral, but the RCD electronics or test circuit can need a specified supply. Follow the exact wiring diagram; Type B does not universally require neutral.

availability.publicTitle: This Simple RCD Error Could Be Deadly!

videos.title: SPD Fundamentals: Transient Surges, Clamping and Device Condition
videos.flowRationale: Separates transient suppression from residual-current and overcurrent protection.
videos.qualification: SPDs limit transients; they do not replace overcurrent or residual-current protection, or protect against every sustained overvoltage. Coordinate Types 1/2/3 and any external lightning protection for the installation. Verify current local requirements.

availability.publicTitle: What is a Surge Protection Device (SPD)? and How Do They Work?

videos.title: Protective-Device Coordination: Selectivity and Discrimination
videos.flowRationale: Compares upstream/downstream devices after their individual principles.
videos.qualification: One plotted overload point does not prove full selectivity. Check the actual fault-current range and manufacturer selectivity/energy tables. Use current RCD verification procedures; the half-rated test discussion is historical.

availability.publicTitle: SELECTIVITY, DISCRIMINATION and CO-ORDINATION of electrical devices for protection

videos.title: Overcurrent Relays: Pickup, Time Delay and Circuit-Breaker Tripping
videos.flowRationale: Clear animated sensor–decision–breaker sequence before motor-specific relays.
videos.qualification: The CT–relay–breaker principle also applies at low voltage. This is a functional introduction, not a relay-testing procedure. Never open an energised CT secondary; testing requires approved isolation and shorting arrangements.

videos.title: Thermal Overload Relays: Motor Current, Trip Contacts and Reset
videos.flowRationale: Explains heating, set current, control contacts and reset before starter applications.
videos.qualification: Normally 95–96 is closed; a trip opens it and closes 97–98. Contact checks do not establish thermal calibration. The relay needs coordinated short-circuit protection. Study detailed starter wiring after motor principles.

availability.publicTitle: What is an Overload Relay? Connection & Working Principle

videos.title: Motor-Protection Circuit Breakers: Thermal, Magnetic and Phase-Loss Mechanisms
videos.flowRationale: Connects thermal, magnetic and phase-loss mechanisms to the breaker family.
videos.qualification: This mechanism is one MPCB design, not a universal feature list. Phase-loss sensitivity is not separate voltage monitoring. Select the current range and short-circuit coordination from the motor nameplate, starting duty and manufacturer data.

availability.publicTitle: How an MPCB Trips: Explained Simply

videos.title: Phase-Monitoring Relays: Phase Failure, Sequence and Voltage Conditions
videos.flowRationale: Finishes by separating voltage/phase supervision from fault-current interruption.
videos.qualification: Functions and thresholds vary by model. The output controls a contactor; it does not interrupt motor fault current. Keep the protective contact effective in every energising path, including while Start is held. Detailed motor wiring follows later.

availability.publicTitle: Understanding Phase Failure Relays | What Are Phase Monitoring Relays?
